newsitem.title: USA: USDA sets final karnal bunt regulations for '96-97.
newsitem.headline: USDA sets final karnal bunt regulations for '96-97.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Tuesday laid out its final regulations to control the karnal bunt wheat durum fungus during the 1996-97 crop year, including double-testing wheat for the disease.

Chiefly, the final regulations create two areas -- restricted areas and surveillance areas -- and set rules for moving wheat from those places. They also establish criteria for planting seed of karnal bunt-host crops, USDA said.
The final rule is slated to be published in the Federal Register October 4 and becomes effective November 4.
The department quarantined wheat in parts of four western states earlier this year after the fungus was discovered.
USDA said wheat moving from restricted areas -- fields that tested positive in the 1996 preharvest survey -- must test negative twice.
It said after this time, the wheat may then move under limited permit to approved milling or storage facilities and is subject to safeguard and sanitation conditions.
USDA defined surveillance areas as those with fields that were associated with contaminated seed or equipment but where the wheat did not test positive in the 1996 preharvest survey.

In its final rule, USDA said wheat moving from surveillance areas must test negative twice and then the grain may be certified for export or unrestricted movement to domestic markets. Safeguard and sanitation conditions were not required.

USDA said fields in the both areas that tested positive during the 1996 harvest or were planted with contaminated seed in 1995 may not be planted in a host crop in the 1996-97 crop season. It said host crops include wheat, durum wheat and triticale, a hybrid of wheat and rye.
